# Audit trail

The record of who changed what: activity per day, filters, the list of changes, one change in full with a readable diff, and revert.

[AuditActivity](#auditactivity) · [AuditFilters](#auditfilters) · [AuditFeed](#auditfeed) · [AuditDiff](#auditdiff) · [AuditEntryPanel](#auditentrypanel)

### AuditActivity

How many changes were made on each day, as bars. The part of a bar that is sensitive (a deletion, a revert, a change to the gate or the pack, a serious decision) is drawn in red, so a day with something to look at stands out. Press a day to see only its changes.

```ts
import { AuditActivity } from '@/contest/components/AuditActivity'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `days` *(required)* | `DayActivity[]` |  | One entry per day, oldest first. See `activityByDay`. |
| `selected` | `string` |  | The day that is chosen, "YYYY-MM-DD". |
| `onSelect` | `(date: string \| undefined) => void` |  | Called with the day that was pressed, or undefined when the chosen day was pressed again. Without it the bars are read-only. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<AuditActivity days={activityByDay(entries, 14, now)} selected={filter.day} onSelect={(day) => setFilter({ ...filter, day })} />
```

- Every bar has a text label ("Oct 29: 3 changes, 1 sensitive"), so the chart can be read without the colours.

### AuditFilters

Narrow the trail: words (they match what was said, who did it and the id), a person, a time range, the kind of thing (in five groups), what was done, and "sensitive only". The line under it says how many of how many are shown, with a button to clear.

```ts
import { AuditFilters } from '@/contest/components/AuditFilters'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` *(required)* | `AuditFilter` |  | The filter. |
| `onChange` *(required)* | `(filter: AuditFilter) => void` |  | Called with the whole new filter. |
| `actors` *(required)* | `string[]` |  | The people who appear in the trail. See `actorsOf`. |
| `total` *(required)* | `number` |  | How many entries there are. |
| `shown` *(required)* | `number` |  | How many pass the filter. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<AuditFilters value={filter} onChange={setFilter} actors={actorsOf(entries)} total={entries.length} shown={filterAudit(entries, filter, now).length} />
```

- The filter itself is plain data (`AuditFilter`) and `filterAudit` applies it, so the same filter works on the server.

### AuditFeed

The trail as a list in groups by day: the time, who, a sentence about what happened, what kind of thing it was, what was done, how many fields changed, a shield when it is sensitive and a mark when it was reverted (the sentence is struck through). It starts with a page of entries and has a button for more.

```ts
import { AuditFeed } from '@/contest/components/AuditFeed'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entries` *(required)* | `AuditEntry[]` |  | The entries to show, newest first. |
| `onSelect` *(required)* | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the id of the entry that was chosen. |
| `now` *(required)* | `number` |  | The clock, in milliseconds. "Today" and "Yesterday" are worked out from it. |
| `all` | `AuditEntry[]` |  | Every entry, to tell which ones were reverted. Defaults to `entries`. |
| `selectedId` | `string \| null` |  | The entry that is open. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `30` | How many entries to show at first and with each "Show more". |
| `empty` | `string` | `'No change matches.'` | Shown when there is nothing to list. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<AuditFeed entries={shown} all={entries} selectedId={id} onSelect={setId} now={now} />
```

### AuditDiff

What an entry changed, as phrases and not as JSON: the name of the field, the value it had and the value it has now. A list of things says what was added, removed and changed in it ("Changed: app-store (Minimum build 372 → 376)"). Added values are green, removed ones red, and each says so in words too.

```ts
import { AuditDiff } from '@/contest/components/AuditDiff'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `changes` *(required)* | `FieldChange[]` |  | What changed, field by field. See `diffEntry`. |
| `empty` | `string` | `'No field changed. The entry records that something happened.'` | Shown when there is nothing to list. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<AuditDiff changes={diffEntry(entry)} />
```

- Fields that always change (times, ids, history lists) are left out. Long text is cut with the full value in the tooltip.

### AuditEntryPanel

One entry in full: who did what to which thing and when, why it is sensitive (if it is), what changed field by field, whether it can be reverted and what a revert would also undo, and the other changes to the same thing. The trail is append-only: a revert is a new entry, never an edit of this one.

```ts
import { AuditEntryPanel } from '@/contest/components/AuditEntryPanel'
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entry` *(required)* | `AuditEntry` |  | The entry. |
| `entries` *(required)* | `AuditEntry[]` |  | Every entry: the panel looks for other changes to the same thing and for a revert. |
| `now` *(required)* | `number` |  | The clock, in milliseconds. |
| `onRevert` *(required)* | `(entry: AuditEntry) => void` |  | Called when the person asks to revert. Ask again before you do it. |
| `onSelect` *(required)* | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the id of another entry chosen in the list of related changes. |
| `busy` | `boolean` |  | Switches the revert button off while a revert is saved. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
<AuditEntryPanel entry={entry} entries={entries} now={now} onSelect={setId} onRevert={setAsking} />
```

- The revert box says what a revert does and how many later changes to the same thing it would undo too. For an entry that cannot be reverted it says why, in words: "Changes to people and scores are kept for the record and cannot be reverted yet."
